title: Linux Desktop Use Surged To 22% On One Workday, Cloudflare Data Shows - Slashdot

content_html:
Cloudflare data suggests desktop Linux usage in North America has climbed to 6.4%, up from 4.1% a year earlier, with one post-holiday workday briefly spiking to 22%. ZDNet reports: [B]elieve it or not, on Monday, July 6, when people were back after the July 4 holiday, Linux usage jumped to a high of 22%. The users of these systems are not AI agents or bots, but real people. I set Cloudflare to count humans rather than bots. If you include people and bots, Linux has a 9.7% market share. That proportion is similar to StatCounter's score. By Cloudflare's count, bots alone come to 19%.

These numbers tell us that workers are leading the way to the Linux desktop. [...] However, past performance doesn't explain present trends. So, why are we now seeing such a bump in Linux desktop growth? Experts believe this trend is largely AI developers and Linux users running AI Agents. For example, as David Linthicum, former managing director and chief cloud strategy officer at Deloitte Consulting and AI and cloud influencer, recently observed, while "Windows 11 can technically run local AI workloads, but as you begin using multiple tools, managing different projects, and installing various dependencies, the friction starts to build," it's a different story for Linux users.

Linthicum continued: "Linux delivered what I can only describe as a true 'AI desktop' experience. Setup was straightforward, mainstream AI instructions matched what you'd actually see in your environment, and GPU-accelerated apps simply worked -- consistently. I spent far less time troubleshooting and far more time actually executing on projects." As for agents, Linux Foundation CEO Jim Zemlin summed up their role succinctly: "Linux is the OS of choice for AI agents."

Desktop Linux is also gaining momentum as frustration with Windows 11 and the end of Windows 10 support push users to alternatives, particularly on older PCs that can't officially upgrade. At the same time, Linux has become much easier to use, install software on, and game with, lowering many of the traditional barriers to switching.

content_html_zh: Cloudflare 数据显示，北美的桌面 Linux 使用率已从一年前的 4.1% 攀升至 6.4%，节后一个工作日短暂飙升至 22%。 ZDNet 报道：不管你信不信，7 月 6 日星期一，当人们在 7 月 4 日假期结束后返回时，Linux 使用率跃升至 22% 的高位。 这些系统的用户不是人工智能代理或机器人，而是真人。 我将 Cloudflare 设置为对人类而不是机器人进行计数。 如果包括人和机器人，Linux 的市场份额为 9.7%。 这个比例与 StatCounter 的分数类似。 根据 Cloudflare 的统计，仅机器人就占 19%。 这些数字告诉我们，工人们正在引领 Linux 桌面的发展。 [...] 然而，过去的表现并不能解释当前的趋势。 那么，为什么我们现在看到 Linux 桌面增长如此迅猛呢？ 专家认为这一趋势主要是人工智能开发者和运行人工智能代理的Linux用户造成的。 例如，正如德勤咨询公司前董事总经理兼首席云战略官、人工智能和云影响者 David Linthicum 最近观察到的那样，虽然“Windows 11 从技术上讲可以运行本地人工智能工作负载，但当你开始使用多种工具、管理不同的项目并安装各种依赖项时，摩擦就会开始增加”，但对于 Linux 用户来说，情况就不同了。 Linthicum 继续说道：“Linux 提供了我只能描述为真正的‘AI 桌面’体验。 设置非常简单，主流 AI 指令与您在环境中实际看到的内容相匹配，GPU 加速的应用程序运行简单且始终如一。 我花在故障排除上的时间少得多，而实际执行项目的时间却多得多。” 至于代理，Linux 基金会首席执行官 Jim Zemlin 简洁地总结了他们的角色：“Linux 是人工智能代理的首选操作系统。” 由于对 Windows 11 的不满以及 Windows 10 支持的终止促使用户转向替代方案，尤其是在无法正式升级的旧电脑上，桌面 Linux 也获得了发展势头。 与此同时，Linux 变得更容易使用、安装软件和玩游戏，降低了许多传统的切换障碍。
